headline: Arabian Vermiculite Industries brings Saudi-made fireproofing to Riyadh
deck: Cementitious sprays and intumescent coatings from a Dammam plant operating since 1985, in a market where the Saudi Building Code decides what can be specified.
excerpt: Arabian Vermiculite Industries, established in Dammam in 1985 under licence from W. R. Grace, is exhibiting sprayed and intumescent structural fire protection at Big 5 Construct Saudi. The company states more than eight million bags of its fireproofing have been applied since 1988 across over 500 major regional projects.
content:
Fire protection is one of the few construction products whose value is only ever demonstrated in failure, which makes it a difficult thing to sell on an exhibition floor and an unusually document-heavy purchase. Arabian Vermiculite Industries, the Dammam manufacturer that has been making sprayed fireproofing in the Kingdom since the mid-1980s, is at Big 5 Construct Saudi this week making that case.

The company was established in 1985 by the Khalifa Al Gosaibi group to produce fireproofing under licence from the American materials group W. R. Grace, at a point when Saudi Arabia's petrochemical and commercial construction programmes were creating demand that imports were serving slowly. Its plant in Dammam produces cementitious and vermiculite-based fire protection alongside vermiculite and perlite products, firestop systems, acoustical spray plasters and horticultural growing media.

Its principal product line is sprayed structural fire protection. Avikote AV-650, the company's Portland cement-based spray and trowel-applied fireproofing, is the type of material applied to structural steel to delay the point at which a section loses load-bearing capacity in a fire, buying the time on which an evacuation strategy and a fire brigade intervention plan depend. The company also supplies intumescent coatings, the thin-film alternative that expands into an insulating char when heated, rated for the protection of structural steel for periods up to two hours.

The distinction matters commercially. Cementitious sprays are cheaper per square metre and durable in industrial and concealed applications; intumescent coatings cost more but preserve the visual profile of exposed steelwork, which is why they dominate architectural projects where the structure is part of the design. Most large Saudi developments now use both, specified section by section.

The company states that more than eight million bags of its fireproofing have been applied since 1988 across more than 500 major projects in the region, and that its product range protects over 2,000 projects in more than 30 countries, spanning building types from hospitals to petrochemical plants. That reference base is the substance of the sales argument: passive fire protection is specified by consultants who will not accept an unproven system, and approval histories on comparable projects carry more weight than product literature.

Regulation is the other driver. Compliance with the Saudi Building Code determines what may be specified and installed, and the code's fire provisions are among the areas where enforcement has tightened as the Kingdom's building stock has grown taller and denser. The Saudi Building Code Center is among the organisations speaking in the conference programme running alongside the exhibition, with sessions addressing navigation of the code.

Demand is being carried by the same pipeline supporting the rest of the show. Saudi construction output is forecast to grow 6.2 per cent this year to about SAR 232.14 billion, and the Saudi Contractors Authority recorded 25 project awards worth more than SR 29.5 billion in June, with building and construction taking 14 of them. Industrial projects add a second stream, since refineries, petrochemical plants and gas facilities carry heavy passive fire protection scopes on structural steel, vessel skirts and pipe racks.

Arabian Vermiculite sits in the industrial portfolio of Khalifa A. Algosaibi Investment, alongside the construction chemicals manufacturer CMCI, the steel foundry SICAST and the training institute ASAS. Big 5 Construct Saudi runs at the Riyadh Front Exhibition and Conference Center until 2 September.
